verdict.rationale: Gitleaks lets users write their own detection rules. Its first-party gitleaks-action runs automatically on pull requests and commits, and when a rule matches it comments on the PR and alerts listed GitHub accounts; a pre-commit hook also blocks commits that contain secrets. However, the actions are fixed (fail, comment, alert) and the triggering events come from GitHub workflows and git hooks, not from a general rule-to-action engine. Missing for 10: user-definable event-to-action rules beyond secret detection, configurable action types (e.g. webhooks or custom remediation), triggers beyond PR/commit, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events
